title: Oscar and the Echo
premise: Paloma Dunmore, a clone of the murdered detective who once ran the long-haul route between the fleet and the silent colony worlds, inherits both her original's unsolved case and her enemies. When the freighter Vespera returns from deep space with its crew aged backward and their memories intact, Paloma realizes the ship is a living record of the Callas Station massacre—an atrocity the fleet has erased from every archive to preserve a fragile truce. As the truce clock runs down, Paloma must protect the de-aged crew, decode the memories the reversal preserved, and expose the fleet admiral who ordered the massacre and now hunts the last evidence. The story ends with Paloma broadcasting the Vespera's testimony fleet-wide, sacrificing her own anonymity and nearly her life, and accepting that she is not her original—but the case, and the truth, are hers now.
about_author: Mirabel Dunmore is the pen name of a former shipping-log archivist who spent a decade cataloguing cargo manifests between orbital habitats before turning to fiction. She writes about people who carry other people's histories, and lives somewhere with very good blackout curtains.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Paloma Dunmore pilots a supply run between the fleet and the colony worlds that severed contact years ago, haunted by the knowledge that she is a copy of a murdered woman. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness and the ache of inherited identity.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Dust
chapters.summary: Sorting her original's belongings, Paloma finds an unfinished murder file on the Callas Station massacre, sealed by fleet order. Her handler, Ives, warns her to burn it. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the pull between safety and obligation.

chapters.title: A Ship Sailing Younger
chapters.summary: The freighter Vespera answers a decades-old distress call, returning with its crew de-aged to childhood while retaining adult minds. Paloma is the nearest ship with clearance to intercept. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was the Captain
chapters.summary: Aboard the Vespera, Paloma meets Captain Okafor, now a child in a captain's body, who insists she witnessed something at Callas Station that officially never happened. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: vertigo at the impossible, and recognition.

chapters.title: What the Fleet Forgot
chapters.summary: Paloma cross-references the Vespera's logs with her original's file and finds the same erasure signature—records not deleted but overwritten with bland falsehoods. POV: Paloma, with an interlude from Okafor's fragmented memories. Emotional beat: the horror of institutional lying.

chapters.title: Ives's Warning
chapters.summary: Ives reveals the truce between the fleet and the colonies expires in forty days, and any scandal could restart the war. He orders Paloma to dock the Vespera at fleet command and say nothing. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: pressure mounting; trust fraying.

chapters.title: Small Bodies, Old Ghosts
chapters.summary: The de-aged crew struggles with children's bodies and adult grief; a young engineer named Tam has a breakdown, remembering a door he was ordered to seal at Callas. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: compassion and the cost of carrying witness.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Smile
chapters.summary: Admiral Rehn Voss, the truce's architect, boards via shuttle, charming and attentive, offering sanctuary for the crew. Paloma recognizes him from her original's file—as the man her original died investigating. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: cold fear beneath a polite mask.

chapters.title: Echo of a Dead Woman
chapters.summary: Voss privately offers Paloma a pardon, a route, a life—if she surrenders the Vespera's memory cores. He calls her by her original's name. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the seduction of being seen, and the trap inside it.

chapters.title: Forty Days
chapters.summary: Paloma refuses, and the Vespera is ordered to fleet custody. She and Okafor plot an unscheduled burn toward the colony worlds, where the massacre's survivors may still live. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: decision crystallizing into defiance.

chapters.title: Running the Silence
chapters.summary: A tense transit through the silent zone between fleet and colonies, pursued by a fleet corvette flying 'assistance' colors. Tam's memories surface in dreams, mapping the station's layout. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: terror and fragile solidarity.

chapters.title: The Colony That Stopped Speaking
chapters.summary: They reach the colony world Meridian, silent for years, and find it not dead but hiding—a whole civilization gone dark to avoid fleet reprisal for sheltering Callas survivors. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: relief shadowed by the depth of the cover-up.

chapters.title: The Survivors' Ledger
chapters.summary: Meridian's elders reveal they keep a handwritten ledger of the dead, names the fleet erased. But the ledger alone proves nothing; they need the Vespera's cores authenticated. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: grief made concrete, one name at a time.

chapters.title: Tam's Door
chapters.summary: Tam leads an expedition to the wreck of Callas Station itself, still drifting in a decaying orbit, to retrieve the physical black box Voss's purge missed. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: confronting the place of the nightmare.

chapters.title: What the Box Says
chapters.summary: The black box confirms it: Voss ordered the station's life support cut during a labor uprising, then reversed the timeline on the Vespera with experimental tech to scramble the witnesses. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: vindication and nausea.

chapters.title: The Corvette Closes
chapters.summary: The fleet corvette catches them at the station; Voss offers one last deal—hand over the box and the crew keeps its pensions and its silence. Okafor, in her child's body, gives a captain's refusal. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: courage from an unexpected quarter.

chapters.title: Truce Expiring
chapters.summary: With hours before the truce lapses, the colonies mobilize on rumor alone, and war feels inevitable. Paloma realizes the only thing that can stop both Voss and the war is the truth, broadcast. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the weight of an impossible choice.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Paloma hijacks the fleet's ceremonial truce channel and plays the black box, the ledger, and Okafor's testimony to every ship in range. Voss's ships power weapons; the colonies hold fire, listening. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the terrifying stillness before judgment.

chapters.title: Voss Unmasked
chapters.summary: Fleet crews mutiny rather than fire on a broadcast of their own dead; Voss attempts to scuttle the Vespera and destroy the last cores, and Paloma stops him at the cost of a decompression injury. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: fury, sacrifice, and the body's price.

chapters.title: A Trial of Records
chapters.summary: A joint fleet-colony tribunal convenes aboard the Vespera; the de-aged crew testify, children's voices carrying old men's memories. Voss is convicted on evidence that can never again be purged. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: solemn, hard-won justice.

chapters.title: New Names, Old Case
chapters.summary: Paloma formally closes her original's file, writing her own name beside it—not as a copy, but as the detective who finished the work. The colonies reopen their channels. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: identity claimed, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Route Ahead
chapters.summary: The Vespera, crew restored to their true ages by Meridian's doctors, joins Paloma on the reopened route between worlds that speak again. She ships the ledger home. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: quiet hope, and a future worth the memory.
